title: Define metering change control process (shadow billing, Finance sign-off, regression review)
creator: Talia Benson
description:
## Why
We have multiple concurrent meter fixes (Hosted API tokens/requests, embeddings batching, cache-hit attribution, Dedicated GPU-seconds v2). Small changes can materially impact invoices, revenue recognition, and experiment readouts. We need a documented change control process that:
- prevents unreviewed meter behavior changes from affecting invoices
- creates an audit trail (who approved what, when, and evidence)
- enforces a shadow-billing compare period for any meter logic/schema change
- standardizes how we treat regressions (incident-style review + rollback/forward-fix plan)

This ticket defines the end-to-end process + required artifacts. Engineering will implement supporting tooling (shadow compare, drift alerts), but this is the governance layer and the operational “how”.

## Scope
Applies to changes that affect any of:
- billed tokens / request counts / embeddings units
- attribution dimensions used for pricing (model, region, customer/account, cache_hit, tier)
- idempotency/dedupe behavior that can change duplicates
- Dedicated usage (GPU-seconds, idle accounting, burst, pool aggregation)
- customer-facing Usage API fields or semantics that could change customer reconciliation

Not in scope:
- cosmetic dashboard UI changes (unless they alter calculation definitions)
- non-billing analytics events that do not feed ledger/invoice exports

## Definitions
**Meter change:** Any code/config/schema change that could alter the quantities used for billing ledger or customer usage exports.

**Shadow billing compare:** Running “old meter” and “new meter” in parallel on the same underlying request stream, producing a diff report, with invoices continuing to use the current production meter.

**Billing-effective date:** Timestamp after which invoices/ledger are allowed to use the new meter version.

## Proposed change control stages
### Stage 0 — Classify the change
Owner (PM/Eng) must classify change as one of:
- A) Non-billing-impacting (no sign-off; still requires changelog entry)
- B) Billing-adjacent (could affect exports/usage API; needs Finance awareness)
- C) Billing-impacting (requires full process below)

Default: if unsure, treat as C.

### Stage 1 — Design + meter spec update
Required artifacts (must be linked in ticket):
1) Updated meter spec section(s) (Confluence) describing the behavior change and examples/edge cases.
2) “Impact hypothesis” (what moves, for whom): expected directionality and magnitude.
3) Rollout plan: shadow window length, segmentation plan for experiments (pre/post), and proposed billing-effective date.

Owners:
- Spec author: Nadia Rahman (metering spec & attribution)
- PM process owner: Chris Osei
- Eng implementation lead: Logan Wright / Cole Summers depending on component

### Stage 2 — Implementation requirements (engineering)
Minimum requirements for any billing-impacting change:
- idempotency/dedupe behavior documented (keys, windows, backfill behavior)
- integration tests updated/added for the changed scenario(s)
- perf-canary scenario added/updated if change affects retries/streaming/fallback
- versioning: meter_version emitted to usage events + ledger export where feasible

### Stage 3 — Shadow billing compare
Shadow compare must run for at least:
- 7 days for Hosted API meter changes OR
- 14 days for Dedicated/GPU-seconds changes (to capture autoscaling/idle patterns)

Shadow compare outputs (required):
- global delta (% and absolute) vs current meter
- breakdown by account, model, region, endpoint type (OpenAI-compat vs native), cache_hit
- discrepancy classification: expected vs suspicious
- top 20 accounts by absolute delta with notes

Guardrails:
- If global delta > 0.5% OR any single account delta > 2% AND not explainable via spec, require escalation and decision before proceed.
- Any increase in duplicate usage event rate, null critical dimensions, or ledger drift beyond SLO thresholds blocks cutover.

### Stage 4 — Approvals (go/no-go)
Approvals required for billing-impacting changes:
- Engineering: Logan Wright (Telemetry EM) confirms implementation + test coverage + rollback plan
- Finance/RevRec: Emily Stone confirms ledger/invoice implications + whether any retroactive adjustments are needed
- Finance sponsor: Laura Bennett sign-off if projected impact is material (threshold TBD; propose >$50k/month or >1% of monthly usage revenue)
- Legal: Sofia Mendes only if customer-facing definitions/contract language changes (e.g., token definition, retries/caching semantics)

Approval evidence must include:
- shadow diff report link
- updated spec link
- confirmation of experiment segmentation plan (avoid mixing meter changes into experiment conclusions)

### Stage 5 — Cutover + monitoring
Cutover checklist:
- announce billing-effective date in #finance_billing + #eng-platform (include meter_version)
- enable alerting on drift vs ledger + duplicates + freshness for first 72h with tighter thresholds
- publish customer-facing notes if usage exports/usage API semantics change (docs + AE FAQ)

Post-cutover validation (owner: Mei Lin / Aisha Bello):
- D+1: confirm drift within threshold across all regions
- D+3: review top accounts reconciliation and support tickets
- D+7: finalize change log entry + close-out note in this ticket

### Stage 6 — Regression handling (incident-style)
If we detect a billing-impacting regression (alerts, customer dispute, or Finance recon):
1) Open an incident channel (or existing on-call process) with clear owner and ETA.
2) Freeze further meter changes until triage complete (unless explicitly exempted).
3) Decide within 24h: rollback vs forward-fix vs leave-as-is.
4) Produce a short postmortem (even if rollback) including:
   - customer impact assessment
   - invoice impact and credit/refund decision path
   - prevention actions (tests, dashboards, process gaps)

## Documentation locations (proposed)
- Confluence: Finance & Legal → RevRec & Billing → “Metering change control” (new page)
- Runbooks: link from SRE alerts to the recon playbook and meter drift runbook
- Linear: this ticket becomes the template/checklist for future meter-change tickets

## Open questions
1) Materiality thresholds for requiring CFO sign-off (propose: >$50k/mo or >1% monthly usage rev; Finance to confirm).
2) Shadow compare duration for small fixes (e.g., single endpoint). Can we shorten to 3 days if delta <0.1% by day 2?
3) Backfills: do we ever backfill billing-impacting fields (e.g., cache_hit) for invoices already issued? Default is no without Finance/Legal approval.
4) Freeze window for month-end close: how does cutover interact with the agreed usage data freeze window?

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Confluence page drafted with the above stages, sign-off matrix, and required artifacts.
- [ ] One “meter change checklist” section that can be copied into new Linear tickets.
- [ ] Alignment from Finance (Emily/Laura) on materiality thresholds + month-end freeze interaction.
- [ ] Alignment from Eng (Logan/Nadia/Cole) that process is implementable with current shadow-billing tooling.
- [ ] Alignment from Legal (Sofia/Michael) on when Legal must review (customer-facing definition changes).

comments: 2026-02-14 — Chris Osei: Drafted initial stages (classification → spec → shadow compare → approvals → cutover). Need Finance input on materiality threshold + month-end freeze interaction. @Talia can you route for sign-off?

2026-02-15 — Emily Stone: From RevRec perspective, biggest risk is retroactive changes without audit trail. Process should explicitly require meter_version + billing-effective date and a policy that we do NOT restate prior invoices unless approved and documented. Also want a required recon export snapshot for the shadow window.

2026-02-16 — Logan Wright: +1. Engineering can support meter_version tagging and shadow compare, but we need the process to be crisp on what blocks cutover (duplicate rate, null dims, ledger drift). Suggest referencing PM-1842 KPIs once finalized.

2026-02-18 — Sofia Mendes: Legal review should be triggered only when customer-facing definitions change (token definition, retries/fallback/caching semantics, dispute/credit wording). Pure bug fixes that reduce overbilling typically don’t need Legal, but any change that could be perceived as “changing what we bill for” should route through us.

2026-02-20 — Laura Bennett: Proposed materiality threshold seems reasonable as a starting point. I want an explicit requirement that Finance gets an invoice preview using the new meter for top 20 accounts before cutover, even if we don’t send it to customers. Also ensure experiment readouts segment pre/post meter fix so we don’t ‘attribute’ pricing effects to meter changes.

2026-02-26 — Talia Benson: Added month-end close interaction section to the draft (freeze window + late events policy). Next step: publish Confluence page and socialize checklist in #finance_billing and #eng-sre; target by 2026-03-04.
